claims.statement: 竜巻は雷雨雲の底から地面まで伸びる、激しく回転する空気の柱である。

evidence.quote:
A tornado is a violently rotating column of air extending from the base of a thunderstorm down to
the ground.

claims.statement: 気象用語集（AMS 2000）では、竜巻は地面に接触し、積雲状の雲から垂れ下がる、激しく回転する空気の柱であり、しばしば漏斗雲として見えるが必ずしもそうとは限らないと定義される。

evidence.quote: air, in contact with the ground, pendant from a cumuliform cloud or underneath a cumuliform cloud,
and often (but not always) visible as a funnel cloud.

claims.statement: 竜巻は地面と対流雲の両方に同時に接触していなければならない。

evidence.quote:
a tornado must be in contact with the ground and a convective cloud at the
same time.

claims.statement: 竜巻は可視の漏斗雲を伴わなくても発生しうる。

evidence.quote: Tornadoes can occur without funnel clouds

claims.statement: 竜巻は丈夫な構造物を完全に破壊し、木を根こそぎにし、物体を致命的な飛来物のように空中へ投げ飛ばすことができる。

evidence.quote: Tornadoes are capable of completely destroying well-made structures, uprooting trees,
hurling objects through the air like deadly missiles

claims.statement: 竜巻は数秒から1時間以上持続しうるが、ほとんどの竜巻は10分未満である。

evidence.quote: Tornadoes can last from several seconds to more than an hour.
Most tornadoes last less than 10 minutes.

claims.statement: 1950年以降の経路長データに基づく竜巻の平均移動距離は約3.5マイルである。

evidence.quote:
average distance tornadoes have traveled (based on path length data since 1950) is about 3-1/2
miles.

claims.statement: 最も破壊的で致命的な竜巻は、メソサイクロンと呼ばれる明確なレーダー循環を持つ回転する雷雨（スーパーセル）から発生する。

evidence.quote: deadly tornadoes occur from supercells--which are rotating thunderstorms with a well-defined radar

evidence.quote: Earth is the only planet in our solar system with only one moon.

claims.statement: 月は地球の自転軸のぐらつきを安定させ、数千年にわたり気候の変動を小さくしてきた。

evidence.quote: It stabilizes our planet's wobble, which has made the climate less variable over

claims.statement: 月は数十億年前、若い地球への大きな岩塊の衝突によって形成された可能性が高い。

claims.statement: 半径1,080マイル（1,738キロメートル）の月は太陽系で5番目に大きな衛星で、地球からの平均距離は238,855マイル（384,400キロメートル）である。

evidence.quote: With a radius of 1,080 miles (1,738 kilometers), the Moon is the fifth largest moon
in our solar system (after Ganymede, Titan, Callisto, and Io).
The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) away from Earth.

claims.statement: 地球は時折、軌道を回る小惑星や大きな岩を一時的に捕らえ、それらは数か月から数年後に太陽を回る軌道へ戻る。

evidence.quote: Earth sometimes temporarily hosts orbiting asteroids or large rocks.

claims.statement: 地球は約45億年前に渦巻くガスと塵が重力で集まって形成され、中心核、岩石のマントル、固体の地殻を持つ。

evidence.quote: When the solar system settled into its current layout about 4.5 billion years ago, Earth formed when
gravity pulled swirling gas and dust in to become the third planet from the Sun.
Earth has a central core, a rocky mantle, and a solid crust.

claims.statement: 地球は中心の内核、外核、マントル、地殻の4つの主要な層からなる。

evidence.quote: Earth is composed of four main layers, starting with an inner core at the planet's center, enveloped
by the outer core, mantle, and crust.

claims.statement: 内核は半径約759マイル（1,221キロメートル）の鉄とニッケルの固体球で、温度は9,800°F（5,400°C）に達する。

evidence.quote: The inner core is a solid sphere made of iron and nickel metals about 759 miles (1,221 kilometers)
in radius. There the temperature is as high as 9,800 degrees Fahrenheit (5,400 degrees Celsius).

claims.statement: 外核は厚さ約1,400マイル（2,300キロメートル）の鉄とニッケルの流体層で、マントルは最も厚い層で約1,800マイル（2,900キロメートル）ある。

evidence.quote: This layer is about 1,400 miles (2,300 kilometers)

the mantle, the thickest layer.

evidence.quote: goes about 19 miles (30 kilometers) deep on average on land.
the crust is thinner and extends about 3 miles (5 kilometers) from the seafloor

claims.statement: 地殻と上部マントルを含むリソスフェアは絶えず動く巨大なプレートに分かれており、プレートの相互作用が地震を引き起こす。

evidence.quote: includes the crust (both continental and oceanic) and the upper mantle, is divided into huge plates
that are constantly moving.
grind past one another, ride up over one another, collide to make mountains, or split and separate.
roughly at a rate equal to the growth of our fingernails.

claims.statement: 地球の全球海洋は表面の約71%を覆い、平均深度約2.3マイル（3.6キロメートル）で、地球の水の97%を含む。

evidence.quote: Earth's global ocean, which covers about 71% of the planet's surface, has an average depth of about
2.3 miles (3.6 kilometers) and contains 97% of Earth's water.
hidden under these oceans.

evidence.quote: Near the surface, Earth has an atmosphere that consists of 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other
gases such as argon, carbon dioxide, and neon.

claims.statement: 大気は地球の気候と天気に影響を与え、有害な太陽放射線の多くを遮り、流星体の大半を大気中で燃え尽きさせる。

evidence.quote: The atmosphere affects Earth's long-term climate and
short-term local weather and shields us from much of the harmful radiation coming from the Sun.
It also protects us from meteoroids, most of which burn up in the atmosphere

claims.statement: 地球の速い自転と溶融したニッケル・鉄の核が磁場を生み出し、太陽風によって宇宙空間で涙滴型に歪められる。

evidence.quote: Our planet's rapid rotation and molten nickel-iron core give rise to a magnetic field, which the
solar wind distorts into a teardrop shape in space.

claims.statement: 太陽風の荷電粒子が地球の磁場に捕らえられると磁極上空で空気分子と衝突し、オーロラを引き起こす。

evidence.quote: When charged particles from the solar wind become trapped in
Earth's magnetic field, they collide with air molecules above our planet's magnetic poles.
molecules then begin to glow and cause aurorae, or the northern and southern lights.

claims.statement: 地球の磁気極性は変化し、磁気反転は平均約30万年ごとに起こるが周期は非常に不規則である。

evidence.quote: the magnetic polarity of Earth can change
a magnetic reversal takes place about every 300,000
years on average, but the timing is very irregular.

claims.statement: 地球の大気は非常に薄く、質量は地球全体の約100万分の1で、約80%が平均12キロメートル（7.5マイル）の対流圏に含まれる。

evidence.quote: Earth’s atmosphere is very thin, with a mass only about one-millionth that of the planet
about 80 percent of the atmosphere is contained within its lowest layer
troposphere, which is, on average, just 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) thick.

it warms our planet and keeps temperatures habitable

claims.statement: 火山は、地下の溶融岩の貯留層につながる火口を中心に築かれた円錐形の丘や山である。

evidence.quote: A volcano is most commonly a conical hill or mountain built around a vent that connects with reservoirs of molten rock below the surface of the Earth.

claims.statement: 地下で火山の通り道を上昇する溶融岩はマグマと呼ばれ、火山から噴出した後は溶岩と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: Molten rock below the surface of the Earth that rises in volcanic vents is known as magma, but after it erupts from a volcano it is called lava.

claims.statement: 溶融岩は周囲の固体岩石より軽く、浮力とガス圧によって上方へ押し上げられ、地殻の弱い帯域を突き破ることがある。

evidence.quote: Driven by buoyancy and gas pressure the molten rock, which is lighter than the surrounding solid rock forces its way upward and may ultimately break though zones of weaknesses in the Earth's crust.

claims.statement: マグマは結晶や未溶融岩石の破片、溶存ガスを含むが、主として酸素・ケイ素・アルミニウム・鉄・マグネシウム・カルシウム・ナトリウム・カリウム・チタン・マンガンからなる液体である。

evidence.quote: the ascending magma commonly contains some crystals, fragments of surrounding (unmelted) rocks, and dissolved gases, but it is primarily a liquid composed principally of oxygen, silicon, aluminum, iron, magnesium, calcium, sodium, potassium, titanium, and manganese.

claims.statement: すべてのマグマは溶存ガスを含み、地表へ向かうにつれて圧力が下がり、ガスは静かにまたは爆発的に放出される。

evidence.quote: All magmas contain dissolved gases, and as they rise to the surface to erupt, the confining pressures are reduced and the dissolved gases are liberated either quietly or explosively.

claims.statement: 溶岩が薄く流動的ならガスは容易に逃げるが、厚く粘稠ならガスが自由に動けず巨大な圧力が溜まり爆発的に放出される。

evidence.quote: If the lava is a thin fluid (not viscous), the gases may escape easily. But if the lava is thick and pasty (highly viscous), the gases will not move freely but will build up tremendous pressure, and ultimately escape with explosive violence.

claims.statement: ガスと溶岩の激しい分離は軽石と呼ばれる岩石の泡を生じ、水に浮くほど軽いものもある。

evidence.quote: The violent separation of gas from lava may produce rock froth called pumice. Some of this froth is so light--because of the many gas bubbles--that it floats on water.

claims.statement: 地表近くで急速に冷えたマグマは、結晶の少ない微細質またはガラス質の火成岩となる。

evidence.quote: If magmas cool rapidly, as might be expected near or on the Earth's surface, they solidify to form igneous rocks that are finely crystalline or glassy with few crystals.

claims.statement: 地表に届かず地下深くにとどまったマグマはゆっくり結晶化し、粗粒でほぼ完全結晶質の火成岩となる。

evidence.quote: If magmas never breach the surface to erupt and remain deep underground, they cool much more slowly and thus allow ample time to sustain crystal precipitation and growth, resulting in the formation of coarser grained, nearly completely crystalline, igneous rocks.

claims.statement: 地質学者は火山を一般に、スコリア丘、成層火山、楯状火山、溶岩ドームの4種類に分類する。

evidence.quote: Geologists generally group volcanoes into four main kinds--cinder cones, composite volcanoes, shield volcanoes, and lava domes.

claims.statement: スコリア丘は最も単純な火山で、単一の火口から噴出した固化した溶岩片で築かれる。

evidence.quote: Cinder cones are the simplest type of volcano. They are built from particles and blobs of congealed lava ejected from a single vent.

claims.statement: ほとんどのスコリア丘は山頂に椀状の火口を持ち、周囲より1,000フィート余り以上高くなることはまれである。

evidence.quote: Most cinder cones have a bowl-shaped crater at the summit and rarely rise more than a thousand feet or so above their surroundings.

claims.statement: 1943年にメキシコのパリクティン近くで始まったスコリア丘は、9年間の活動で約100平方マイルを灰で覆い、サンファンの町を破壊した。

evidence.quote: In 1943 a cinder cone started growing on a farm near the village of Parícutin in Mexico.
During 9 years of activity, Parícutin built a prominent cone, covered about 100 square miles with ashes, and destroyed the town of San Juan.

claims.statement: 成層火山は溶岩流・火山灰・スコリア・岩塊・火山弾の互層からなる急斜面の対称的な大円錐で、麓から8,000フィートもそびえることがある。

evidence.quote: They are typically steep-sided, symmetrical cones of large dimension built of alternating layers of lava flows, volcanic ash, cinders, blocks, and bombs and may rise as much as 8,000 feet above their bases.

claims.statement: 楯状火山はほぼ完全に流動性の溶岩流で築かれ、戦士の盾に似た幅広くなだらかな円錐を形成する。

evidence.quote: Shield volcanoes, the third type of volcano, are built almost entirely of fluid lava flows.
building a broad, gently sloping cone of flat, domical shape, with a profile much like that of a warrior's shield

claims.statement: 最大の楯状火山マウナロアは海抜13,677フィートで、山頂は深い海底から28,000フィート以上の高さにあたる。

evidence.quote: As Mauna Loa, the largest of the shield volcanoes (and also the world's largest active volcano), projects 13,677 feet above sea level, its top is over 28,000 feet above the deep ocean floor.

claims.statement: 溶岩ドームは遠くまで流れられない粘性の高い溶岩が火口の上に盛り上がってでき、主に内部からの膨張で成長する。

evidence.quote: Volcanic or lava domes are formed by relatively small, bulbous masses of lava too viscous to flow any great distance; consequently, on extrusion, the lava piles over and around its vent.
A dome grows largely by expansion from within.

claims.statement: カルデラは直径1〜15マイルのほぼ円形の窪地から、長さ60マイルにもなる細長い窪地まで多様である。

evidence.quote: Calderas range in form and size from roughly circular depressions 1 to 15 miles in diameter to huge elongated depressions as much as 60 miles long.

claims.statement: クレーターレイクは約6,800年前の一連の大爆発の後に火山の頂部が崩壊して形成された。

evidence.quote: Following a series of tremendous explosions about 6,800 years ago, the volcano lost its top.
Depressions such as Crater Lake, formed by collapse of volcanoes, are known as calderas.

claims.statement: 火山灰は燃焼の産物ではなく、直径2ミリから0.004ミリ未満の岩石・鉱物・火山ガラスの破片からなる。

evidence.quote: Volcanic ash is not the product of combustion, like the soft fluffy material created by burning wood, leaves, or paper, but rather consists of fragments of rocks, minerals, and volcanic glass ranging in size from sand to clay-like (from 2 mm (1/12 in) to less than 0.004 mm (1/256th in) in diameter).

claims.statement: 火山灰は硬く研磨性があり、弱い腐食性を持ち、湿ると電気を通し、水に溶けない。

evidence.quote: Ash is hard, abrasive, mildly corrosive, conducts electricity when wet, and does not dissolve in water.

claims.statement: 風は小さな火山灰粒子を火山から数十〜数千キロメートル先まで運ぶことがある。

evidence.quote: Wind can then blow the tiny ash particles tens to thousands of kilometers away from the volcano.

claims.statement: 噴火様式はマグマの特性と噴出量・噴出率で決まり、低粘度玄武岩質マグマの溶岩流から高粘度でガスに富む流紋岩質・デイサイト質マグマの爆発的噴火まで幅がある。

evidence.quote: The style of a volcanic eruption is controlled by the characteristics of the erupting magma (molten rock), and the volume of and rate at which the magma is emitted.
eruption styles range from (1) effusion of lava flows and eruption of lava fountains that produce very little ash, and is typical of eruptions of low-viscosity basaltic magma
extremely explosive eruptions that inject large quantities of ash high into the stratosphere, typical of eruptions of rhyolite and dacite magma that are highly viscous and gas-rich

claims.statement: 1902年にモン・ペレの噴火で、約4マイル下流のサンピエールが白熱した高速の灰流と熱いガス・火山塵によって破壊され、約3万人が死亡した。

evidence.quote: An extremely destructive eruption accompanied the growth of a dome at Mont Pelée in 1902.

The coastal town of St. Pierre, about 4 miles downslope to the south, was demolished and nearly 30,000 inhabitants were killed by an incandescent, high-velocity ash flow and associated hot gases and volcanic dust.

claims.statement: 爆発的噴火は、マグマ中の溶存ガスが膨張して激しく逃げるか、水がマグマに熱せられて急激に水蒸気となることで起こる。

evidence.quote: Explosive eruptions occur when gases dissolved in molten rock (magma) expand as the magma rises, and then escape violently into the air, or when water is heated by magma and abruptly flashes into steam.

claims.statement: 最も細かい火山灰は成層圏の風に乗って地球を何周もしてから降着することがある。

evidence.quote: The finest ash particles may be injected miles into the atmosphere and carried many times around the world by stratospheric winds before settling out.

claims.statement: 津波は、海洋の大規模で突然の変位によって発生する一連の長い波である。

evidence.quote: Tsunamis are a series of long waves generated by a large and sudden displacement of the ocean.

claims.statement: 海底またはその近くの大地震が津波の最も一般的な原因だが、地すべり、火山活動、特定の気象、隕石も津波を起こしうる。

evidence.quote: Large earthquakes below or near the ocean floor are the most common cause, but landslides, volcanic activity, certain types of weather, and meteorites can also cause a tsunami.

claims.statement: 津波は「潮波」と呼ばれることがあるが、潮汐とは関係がなく誤解を招く。

evidence.quote: Tsunamis are sometimes referred to as "tidal waves", but this is very misleading as they are not related to tides.

claims.statement: 津波は発生源から全方位に放射状に広がり、海洋盆地全体を横断することがある。

evidence.quote: Tsunamis radiate outward in all directions from their source and can move across entire ocean basins.

claims.statement: 沿岸に達した津波は、数時間から数日続く危険な沿岸洪水と強い海流を引き起こす。

evidence.quote: When they reach the coast, they can cause dangerous coastal flooding and powerful currents that can last for several hours or days.

claims.statement: 1850年以降、津波は世界中で数十万人の命を奪い、数千億ドルの被害をもたらした。

evidence.quote: Since 1850, tsunamis have claimed hundreds of thousands of lives and caused hundreds of billions of dollars in damage around the world.

claims.statement: 津波はどの海洋沿岸にもいつでも襲来しうるもので、津波に季節はない。

evidence.quote: A tsunami can strike any ocean coast at any time. There is no season for tsunamis.

claims.statement: 「津波」という語は、日本語で「港の波」を意味する文字に由来する。

evidence.quote: The word "tsunami," pronounced (soo-NAH-mee) comes from the Japanese characters meaning "harbor wave."

claims.statement: 世界のすべての海洋沿岸のコミュニティが津波のリスクを抱えており、津波は自然界で最も強力で破壊的な力の一つである。

evidence.quote: Communities along the coasts of all the world's oceans are at risk from tsunamis. They are one of nature's most powerful and destructive forces.

claims.statement: 津波の速度は、重力加速度（毎秒毎秒32.2フィート、9.8メートル）と水深の積の平方根で計算できる。

evidence.quote: Tsunami speed can be computed by taking the square root of the product of the acceleration of gravity, which is 32.2 feet (9.8 meters) per second squared, and water depth.

claims.statement: 水深15,000フィート（4,600メートル）では、津波の速度はほぼ時速475マイル（765キロメートル）になる。

evidence.quote: In 15,000 feet (4,600 meters) of water, this works out to almost 475 mph (765 km/h).

claims.statement: 津波はアリューシャン列島からハワイまで約5時間、ポルトガル沿岸からノースカロライナまで8時間半で進む。

evidence.quote: At rates like this, a tsunami will travel from Alaska's Aleutian Islands to Hawaii in about five hours; or from the Portugal coast to North Carolina in eight and a half hours.

claims.statement: 風波が海洋の表層だけに影響するのと異なり、津波は海面から海底までの水柱全体を通じて伝わる。

evidence.quote: Unlike wind waves that affect just the surface of the ocean, tsunamis propagate (move) through the entire depth of the ocean, from the surface to the floor.

claims.statement: 深海では津波はジェット機並みの時速500マイル（800キロメートル）超で進み、1日足らずで大洋全体を横断できる。

evidence.quote: In the deep ocean, tsunamis can move as fast as a jet plane, over 500 mph (800 km/h), and can cross entire oceans in less than a day.

claims.statement: 津波の波長は数百マイルにもなるため、深海ではほとんど目立たず、高さは3フィート（1メートル）を超えることはめったにない。

evidence.quote: Because of a tsunami's long wavelengths, which can be hundreds of miles, a tsunami is barely noticeable in the deep ocean and rarely more than three feet (one meter) high.

claims.statement: 海上の船員は通常、船体の下を通過する津波に気づかない。

evidence.quote: Mariners at sea will not normally notice a tsunami as it passes beneath their hulls.

claims.statement: 陸に近い浅瀬に入ると津波は減速し、波長が縮み、波高が増し、海流が強まる。

evidence.quote: As a tsunami enters shallow water near land, it slows down, wavelengths decrease, waves grow in height, and currents intensify.

claims.statement: 岸では多くの津波が自動車並みの時速20〜30マイル（30〜50キロメートル）まで減速する。

evidence.quote: At the shore, most tsunamis slow to the speed of a car, approximately 20 to 30 mph (30 to 50 km/h).

claims.statement: 津波は海底の地震または海底火山の噴火によって引き起こされる巨大な波である。

evidence.quote: Tsunamis are giant waves caused by earthquakes or volcanic eruptions under the sea.

claims.statement: 津波の速度は発生源からの距離ではなく海洋の深さに依存する。

evidence.quote: The speed of tsunami waves depends on ocean depth rather than the distance from the source of the wave.

claims.statement: 2009年9月29日、南太平洋の大地震で発生した津波が米領サモア、サモア、トンガに大きな被害と犠牲をもたらした。

evidence.quote: On September 29, 2009, a tsunami caused substantial damage and loss of life in American Samoa, Samoa, and Tonga. The tsunami was generated by a large earthquake in the Southern Pacific Ocean.

claims.statement: 潮汐はこれらの巨大な波とほとんど関係がないため、海洋学者は「潮波」という呼称を推奨していない。

evidence.quote: While tsunamis are often referred to as tidal waves, this name is discouraged by oceanographers because tides have little to do with these giant waves.

claims.statement: 地質学でプレートとは硬い固体岩石の大きな板であり、テクトニクスはギリシャ語の「建てる」に由来する。

evidence.quote: In geologic terms, a plate is a large, rigid slab of solid rock. The word tectonics comes from the Greek root "to build."

claims.statement: プレートテクトニクス理論は、地球の最外層が互いに相対的に動く大小12枚以上のプレートに分かれ、より高温で動きやすい物質の上に乗っていると主張する。

evidence.quote: The theory of plate tectonics states that the Earth's outermost layer is fragmented into a dozen or more large and small plates that are moving relative to one another as they ride atop hotter, more mobile material.

claims.statement: 超大陸パンゲアは約2億2,500万〜2億年前に分裂を始め、現在の大陸へと分かれた。

evidence.quote: the supercontinent Pangaea began to break up about 225-200 million years ago, eventually fragmenting into the continents as we know them today.

claims.statement: 大陸が現在の位置に固定されていないという考えは、1596年にオランダの地図製作者アブラハム・オルテリウスが『テサウルス・ゲオグラフィクス』で最初に示唆した。

evidence.quote: this notion was first suggested as early as 1596 by the Dutch map maker Abraham Ortelius in his work Thesaurus Geographicus.

claims.statement: 移動する大陸の考えが本格的な科学理論として取り上げられたのは1912年で、32歳のドイツの気象学者アルフレート・ローター・ヴェーゲナーが2編の論文で大陸移動説を発表した。

evidence.quote: it was not until 1912 that the idea of moving continents was seriously considered as a full-blown scientific theory -- called Continental Drift -- introduced in two articles published by a 32-year-old German meteorologist named Alfred Lothar Wegener.

claims.statement: 南アメリカとアフリカの沿岸部の同一化石種の存在、南極の熱帯植物化石、乾燥アフリカの氷河堆積物が、大陸がかつて結合していた証拠とされた。

evidence.quote: To him, the presence of identical fossil species along the coastal parts of Africa and South America was the most compelling evidence that the two continents were once joined.
the discovery of fossils of tropical plants (in the form of coal deposits) in Antarctica led to the conclusion that this frozen land previously must have been situated closer to the equator
the occurrence of glacial deposits in present-day arid Africa

claims.statement: ヴェーゲナー理論は大陸を動かす力を説明できず、地球物理学者ハロルド・ジェフリーズは固体岩石の大きな塊が破壊されずに大洋底を押し進むことは物理的に不可能だと正しく論じた。

evidence.quote: A fatal weakness in Wegener's theory was that it could not satisfactorily answer the most fundamental question raised by his critics: What kind of forces could be strong enough to move such large masses of solid rock over such great distances?
argued correctly that it was physically impossible for a large mass of solid rock to plow through the ocean floor without breaking up.

claims.statement: ヴェーゲナーは1930年にグリーンランド氷冠の横断探検中に凍死したが、没後の海底探査の新証拠が理論への関心を再燃させ、プレートテクトニクスの理論へ発展した。

evidence.quote: He froze to death in 1930 during an expedition crossing the Greenland ice cap, but the controversy he spawned raged on.
after his death, new evidence from ocean floor exploration and other studies rekindled interest in Wegener's theory, ultimately leading to the development of the theory of plate tectonics.

claims.statement: プレートテクトニクスは地球科学において、物理学・化学における原子構造の発見や生命科学における進化論と同程度に重要であることが証明された。

evidence.quote: Plate tectonics has proven to be as important to the earth sciences as the discovery of the structure of the atom was to physics and chemistry and the theory of evolution was to the life sciences.

claims.statement: この理論は古生物学から地震学まで地球科学の多くの分野を統合し、地震や火山噴火が特定地域に集中する理由や大山脈の成因を説明した。

evidence.quote: It has provided explanations to questions that scientists had speculated upon for centuries -- such as why earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur in very specific areas around the world, and how and why great mountain ranges like the Alps and Himalayas formed.
The theory has unified the study of the Earth by drawing together many branches of the earth sciences, from paleontology (the study of fossils) to seismology (the study of earthquakes).

claims.statement: プレートを推進する力の本性は、ヴェーゲナーが解決できなかった問いであり、今日も主要な未解決問題の一つである。

evidence.quote: one of the chief outstanding questions is the one Wegener failed to resolve: What is the nature of the forces propelling the plates?

claims.statement: プレートテクトニクスに似た過程が他の惑星で働くか、働いたことがあるかも議論されている。

evidence.quote: whether similar processes operate, or have ever operated, on other planets in our solar system.

claims.statement: プレートの運動の大部分はプレート間の狭い帯域で起こり、境界には発散・収束・トランスフォーム・境界帯の4種類がある。

evidence.quote: Most movement occurs along narrow zones between plates where the results of plate-tectonic forces are most evident.
There are four types of plate boundaries:

claims.statement: 発散境界はプレートが離れていく拡大中心に沿って存在し、マントルから押し上がるマグマによって新しい地殻が作られる。

evidence.quote: Divergent boundaries occur along spreading centers where plates are moving apart and new crust is created by magma pushing up from the mantle.

claims.statement: 中央大西洋海嶺の拡大率は平均で年2.5センチメートル、100万年で25キロメートルである。

evidence.quote: The rate of spreading along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge averages about 2.5 centimeters per year (cm/yr), or 25 km in a million years.

claims.statement: 過去1〜2億年の海底拡大が、大西洋をヨーロッパ・アフリカ・南北アメリカの間の小さな入り江から現在の巨大な大洋へ成長させた。

evidence.quote: Seafloor spreading over the past 100 to 200 million years has caused the Atlantic Ocean to grow from a tiny inlet of water between the continents of Europe, Africa, and the Americas into the vast ocean that exists today.

claims.statement: 地球の大きさは過去6億年間でほとんど変わっていないため地殻は生成とほぼ同じ速度で破壊され、プレートが沈み込む場所は沈み込み帯と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: The size of the Earth has not changed significantly during the past 600 million years

Such destruction (recycling) of crust takes place along convergent boundaries where plates are moving toward each other, and sometimes one plate sinks (is subducted) under another. The location where sinking of a plate occurs is called a subduction zone.

claims.statement: 約5,000万年前のインドのアジアへの衝突がインド・ユーラシア両プレートを衝突帯で圧潰させ、ヒマラヤとチベット高原を押し上げた。

evidence.quote: The collision of India into Asia 50 million years ago caused the Indian and Eurasian Plates to crumple up along the collision zone.
the slow continuous convergence of these two plates over millions of years pushed up the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau to their present heights.

claims.statement: 1994年6月9日、ボリビアのラパス北東約320キロで深さ636キロのマグニチュード8.3の地震が発生した。

evidence.quote: On 9 June 1994, a magnitude-8.3 earthquake struck about 320 km northeast of La Paz, Bolivia, at a depth of 636 km.

claims.statement: マリアナ海溝南端のチャレンジャー海淵は約11,000メートルに達し、エベレストの海抜約8,854メートルよりも深く地球内部へ入り込む。

evidence.quote: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Marianas Trench, plunges deeper into the Earth's interior (nearly 11,000 m) than Mount Everest, the world's tallest mountain, rises above sea level (about 8,854 m).

claims.statement: トランスフォーム断層の概念はカナダの地球物理学者J・トゥーゾ・ウィルソンに始まり、長さ約1,300キロのサンアンドレアス断層帯では太平洋プレートが北アメリカプレートの横を1,000万年にわたり年平均約5センチでずれてきた。

evidence.quote: The concept of transform faults originated with Canadian geophysicist J. Tuzo Wilson
Most transform faults are found on the ocean floor.

The San Andreas fault zone, which is about 1,300 km long and in places tens of kilometers wide, slices through two thirds of the length of California. Along it, the Pacific Plate has been grinding horizontally past the North American Plate for 10 million years, at an average rate of about 5 cm/yr.

claims.statement: プレート分離の平均速度は北極海嶺の年2.5センチメートル未満から東太平洋海膨の年15センチメートル超まで幅がある。

evidence.quote: The Arctic Ridge has the slowest rate (less than 2.5 cm/yr), and the East Pacific Rise near Easter Island, in the South Pacific about 3,400 km west of Chile, has the fastest rate (more than 15 cm/yr).

claims.statement: 現在のプレート運動はVLBI・衛星レーザー測距・GPSという宇宙測地技術で追跡され、数年間の平均速度と方向は数百万年の平均とよく一致する。

evidence.quote: The three most commonly used space-geodetic techniques -- very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), satellite laser ranging (SLR), and the Global Positioning System (GPS)

Space-geodetic data have already confirmed that the rates and direction of plate movement, averaged over several years, compare well with rates and direction of plate movement averaged over millions of years.

claims.statement: 地震と火山噴火の大半はプレート境界近くで起こるが、ハワイ諸島は最近のプレート境界から3,200キロ以上離れた太平洋中央に形成された例外である。

evidence.quote: The vast majority of earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur near plate boundaries, but there are some exceptions.
the Hawaiian Islands, which are entirely of volcanic origin, have formed in the middle of the Pacific Ocean more than 3,200 km from the nearest plate boundary.

claims.statement: 1963年にJ・トゥーゾ・ウィルソンが「ホットスポット」理論を考案し、ハワイ諸島・天皇海山群の直線形は太平洋プレートが深い定常ホットスポット上を移動した結果だと仮説した。

evidence.quote: In 1963, J. Tuzo Wilson, the Canadian geophysicist who discovered transform faults, came up with an ingenious idea that became known as the "hotspot" theory.
Wilson hypothesized that the distinctive linear shape of the Hawaiian Island-Emperor Seamounts chain resulted from the Pacific Plate moving over a deep, stationary hotspot in the mantle

claims.statement: カウアイ島の最古の火山岩は約550万年前で深く浸食されている一方、ホットスポット上にあるとされるハワイ島の露出岩石は70万年未満で新しい火山岩が形成され続けている。

evidence.quote: The oldest volcanic rocks on Kauai, the northwesternmost inhabited Hawaiian island, are about 5.5 million years old and are deeply eroded.
the oldest exposed rocks are less than 0.7 million years old and new volcanic rock is continually being formed.

claims.statement: 過去1,000万年間に地殻の下で100以上のホットスポットが活動したと考えられている。

evidence.quote: More than a hundred hotspots beneath the Earth's crust have been active during the past 10 million years.

claims.statement: イエローストーンのホットスポットとされる熱エネルギーは、1万以上の熱水鉱泉・間欠泉・泥沸泉を賄う。

evidence.quote: The thermal energy of the presumed Yellowstone hotspot fuels more than 10,000 hot pools and springs, geysers (like Old Faithful), and bubbling mudpots (pools of boiling mud).

claims.statement: 新しい研究は、ホットスポットが深部の現象でも位置が固定されたものでもないと示唆し、プルームモデルの仮定を問い直している。

evidence.quote: New studies suggest that hotspots are neither deep phenomena nor "fixed" in position over geologic time, as assumed in the popular plume model.

claims.statement: 氷河は、長年にわたり降り積もった雪が圧縮されて大きく厚い氷の塊となることでできる。

evidence.quote: Glaciers are made up of fallen snow that, over many years, compresses into large, thickened ice masses.

claims.statement: 圧縮された雪が溶けなければ、やがて氷河氷となり氷河へと変わる。

evidence.quote: Over time and as more snow falls, if the compressed snow doesn’t melt, the snow eventually becomes glacial ice, transforming into a glacier.

claims.statement: 氷河はその巨大な質量のため、ごく遅い川のように流れる。

evidence.quote: Due to their sheer mass, glaciers flow like very slow rivers.

claims.statement: 氷河の上面は底面より速く動き、底面は地面との摩擦で減速される。

evidence.quote: The top of the glacier moves faster than the underside because the underside is slowed by the friction created as it slides along the ground’s surface.

claims.statement: 十分に長い期間の多量の降雪は氷河の質量を増やして前進させ、長期の温暖化は融解を増やして後退させる。

evidence.quote: Greater amounts of snowfall accumulating over a long enough time will add to the mass of a glacier, causing it to advance. Warmer temperatures over a long enough time will result in more of the glacier ice and snow on the glacier melting, causing it to retreat.

claims.statement: 1986年にアラスカのハバード氷河は1日10メートル（32フィート）の速さで急進し、わずか2か月でラッセルフィヨルドの水を堰き止めて湖を作った。

evidence.quote: Some glaciers may surge, racing forward at several meters per day for weeks or even months. The Hubbard Glacier in Alaska surged at the rate of 10 meters (32 feet) per day in 1986. In only two months, the glacier dammed water in the Russell Fjord and created a lake.

claims.statement: 現在、氷河は世界の陸地総面積の約10％を占め、大半は南極・グリーンランド・カナダ北極圏などの極域にある。

evidence.quote: Today, glaciers occupy about ten percent of the world’s total land area, with most located in polar regions like Antarctica, Greenland, and the Canadian Arctic.

claims.statement: 最終氷期には、氷が陸地の約32％、海洋の約30％を覆っていた。

evidence.quote: Glaciers can be thought of as remnants from the last Ice Age, when ice covered nearly 32 percent of the land and 30 percent of the oceans.

claims.statement: 過去75万年以内に、間氷期と呼ばれる温暖期で隔てられた8回の氷期サイクルがあった。

evidence.quote: within the past 750,000 years, there have been eight Ice Age cycles, separated by warmer periods called interglacial periods.

claims.statement: 氷河は陸上の比較的恒久的な氷の形成物であり、氷山は水上の比較的短命な自由浮遊氷体で、氷河から裂けてできることが多い。

evidence.quote: While a glacier is a relatively permanent ice formation on land, an iceberg is a comparatively short-lived free-floating body of ice on water. Icebergs typically form when chunks of ice break off of a glacier.

claims.statement: 氷河氷の年代は数百年から数十万年に及び、科学者は氷河や氷床からアイスコアを掘削して長期的な気候記録を得る。

evidence.quote: Glacial ice can range in age from several hundred to several hundreds of thousands of years old, making it an invaluable tool for scientific research. To see a long-term climate record, scientists drill and extract ice cores from glaciers and ice sheets.

claims.statement: 氷河はアイスコア内の小さな気泡に数千年前の大気の断片を保存し、過去の大気の状態・気温変動・植生を明らかにする。

evidence.quote: Glaciers preserve bits of atmosphere from thousands of years ago in tiny air bubbles trapped within the ice cores. These can reveal past atmospheric conditions, temperature variations, and types of vegetation.

claims.statement: 20世紀初頭以来、ほとんど例外なく世界中の氷河が前例のない速さで後退している。

evidence.quote: Since the early twentieth century, with few exceptions, glaciers around the world have been retreating at unprecedented rates.

claims.statement: アラスカのミューア氷河は60年余りで7マイル（12キロメートル）以上後退し、800メートル（2,600フィート）以上薄くなった。

evidence.quote: In the span of just over 60 years, the glacier retreated by more than seven miles (12 kilometers) and thinned by more than 800 meters (2,600 feet).

claims.statement: 世界氷河目録（WGI）は13万を超える氷河の情報を収録している。

evidence.quote: The WGI contains information for over 130,000 glaciers.

claims.statement: 山岳氷河、特にアラスカの氷河は、海面水位の上昇とその世界的影響に大きく寄与している。

evidence.quote: Mountain glaciers, particularly in Alaska, contribute significantly to sea level rise and its global implications

claims.statement: 氷河は夏期後半に融水を放出し、春の融雪と秋の雨の間の河川流量を維持する。

evidence.quote: Glaciers release melt water during the late summer season, which sustains streamflow between spring snow melt and fall rain

claims.statement: 氷河は下流の生態系と生物学的に結びつき、サケに不可欠な冷水を供給している。

evidence.quote: Glaciers are biologically linked to their downstream ecosystems, providing cold water critical for salmon

claims.statement: USGSのベンチマーク氷河サイトは5か所で、中〜高緯度にまたがり内陸から沿岸まで気候的に異なる地域を代表する。

evidence.quote: Five U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Benchmark Glacier sites span mid to high latitudes and represent climatically distinct regions, from inland to coastal

claims.statement: USGSの科学者は毎年春と秋に同じベンチマーク氷河サイトを訪れ、降雪量と雪氷の融解を直接測定する。

evidence.quote: USGS scientists visit the same Benchmark Glacier sites every spring and fall to make direct measurements of snow accumulation and snow and ice melt.

claims.statement: 海に届く前に、氷河の融水は人間の飲料・農業・レクリエーション・水力発電に淡水を供給する。

evidence.quote: Before reaching the sea, glacier melt provides freshwater for human consumption, agriculture, recreation, and hydropower.

claims.statement: 水循環において、氷河の氷は海洋に次ぐ第2の水の貯留層である。

evidence.quote: the critically important hydrologic cycle, in which glacier ice is the second largest reservoir of water after the oceans.

claims.statement: 地すべりとは、岩・土壌・人工の盛土またはその組み合わせを含む斜面構成材料の下方・外方への移動をもたらす広範な過程群である。

evidence.quote: The term "landslide" describes a wide variety of processes that result in the downward and outward movement of slope-forming materials including rock, soil, artificial fill, or a combination of these.

claims.statement: 地すべりの材料は、墜落・転倒・滑動・拡散・流動によって動きうる。

evidence.quote: The materials may move by falling, toppling, sliding, spreading, or flowing.

claims.statement: 地すべりは主に山岳地域と結びつけられるが、起伏の少ない地域でも発生しうる。

evidence.quote: Although landslides are primarily associated with mountainous regions, they can also occur in areas of generally low relief.

claims.statement: 米国の地すべりは全50州で発生し、主な発生・潜在地域はカリフォルニア・オレゴン・ワシントンの沿岸・山岳部、内陸西部諸州、東部の山岳・丘陵地域であり、アラスカとハワイも全種類の地すべりを経験する。

evidence.quote: Landslides in the United States occur in all 50 States. The primary regions of landslide occurrence and potential are the coastal and mountainous areas of California, Oregon, and Washington, the States comprising the intermountain west, and the mountainous and hilly regions of the Eastern United States. Alaska and Hawaii also experience all types of landslides.

claims.statement: 米国の地すべりは年間約35億ドル（2001年ドル）の被害を与え、年間25〜50人を死亡させる。

evidence.quote: Landslides in the United States cause approximately $3.5 billion (year 2001 dollars) in damage, and kill between 25 and 50 people annually.

claims.statement: 狭義の滑落（スライド）は、滑動材料と下の安定材料を分ける明確な弱層帯がある塊移動であり、回転型と並進型が主要な2型である。

evidence.quote: the more restrictive use of the term refers only to mass movements, where there is a distinct zone of weakness that separates the slide material from more stable underlying material. The two major types of slides are rotational slides and translational slides.

claims.statement: 落石は急斜面や崖から分離した岩・巨石の急激な動きで、自由落下・跳ね返り・転がりで移動し、重力・機械的風化・間隙水に強く影響される。

evidence.quote: Falls are abrupt movements of masses of geologic materials, such as rocks and boulders, that become detached from steep slopes or cliffs
movement occurs by free-fall, bouncing, and rolling. Falls are strongly influenced by gravity, mechanical weathering, and the presence of interstitial water.

claims.statement: 転倒破壊は、重力と隣接単位または亀裂内の流体が及ぼす力の下で、単位内部の低い支点を中心とした前方回転である。

evidence.quote: Toppling failures are distinguished by the forward rotation of a unit or units about some pivotal point, below or low in the unit, under the actions of gravity and forces exerted by adjacent units or by fluids in cracks

claims.statement: デブリフローは緩い土・岩・有機物・空気・水がスラリー状になって斜面を下る急速な塊移動で、激しい降水や急速な融雪による表層水流が急斜面の緩い土や岩を浸食・移動させることで起こる。

evidence.quote: A debris flow is a form of rapid mass movement in which a combination of loose soil, rock, organic matter, air, and water mobilize as a slurry that flows downslope
Debris flows are commonly caused by intense surface-water flow, due to heavy precipitation or rapid snowmelt, that erodes and mobilizes loose soil or rock on steep slopes.

claims.statement: 斜面の植生を失わせる火災は、デブリフローへの感受性を高める。

evidence.quote: Fires that denude slopes of vegetation intensify the susceptibility of slopes to debris flows.

claims.statement: 泥流は少なくとも50％の砂・シルト・粘土粒径の粒子を含む急速に流れるほど湿った土石流であり、泥流とデブリフローは報道で「マッドスライド」と呼ばれることも多い。

evidence.quote: A mudflow is an earthflow consisting of material that is wet enough to flow rapidly and that contains at least 50 percent sand-, silt-, and clay-sized particles.
mudflows and debris flows are commonly referred to as "mudslides."

claims.statement: クリープは、永久変形を生じるのに十分だが剪断破壊には小さすぎる剪断応力による知覚できないほど遅い定常的な下方運動で、湾曲した樹幹・曲がった柵・傾いた電柱・小さな土の波状起伏で示される。

evidence.quote: Creep is the imperceptibly slow, steady, downward movement of slope-forming soil or rock. Movement is caused by shear stress sufficient to produce permanent deformation, but too small to produce shear failure.
Creep is indicated by curved tree trunks, bent fences or retaining walls, tilted poles or fences, and small soil ripples or ridges

claims.statement: 側方拡散は緩斜面や平坦地で起こり、飽和した緩い非粘性堆積物が固相から液化状態へ変わる液状化が原因で、通常地震のような急速な地動が誘因となる。

evidence.quote: The failure is caused by liquefaction, the process whereby saturated, loose, cohesionless sediments (usually sands and silts) are transformed from a solid into a liquefied state. Failure is usually triggered by rapid ground motion, such as that experienced during an earthquake, but can also be artificially induced.

claims.statement: 水による斜面飽和は地すべりの主原因であり、激しい降雨・融雪・地下水位の変化・海岸線や土ダム・湖沼・溜池・運河・河川の水際の水位変化の形で起こりうる。

evidence.quote: Slope saturation by water is a primary cause of landslides. This effect can occur in the form of intense rainfall, snowmelt, changes in ground-water levels, and water-level changes along coastlines, earth dams, and the banks of lakes, reservoirs, canals, and rivers.

claims.statement: 地すべりと洪水は降水・流出・地盤の水飽和を通じて密接に結びつき、小さな急な渓流で起こるデブリフローや泥流は洪水と誤認されることが多い。

evidence.quote: Landsliding and flooding are closely allied because both are related to precipitation, runoff, and the saturation of ground by water. In addition, debris flows and mudflows usually occur in small, steep stream channels and often are mistaken for floods; in fact, these two events often occur simultaneously in the same area.

claims.statement: 地すべりは谷や渓流を堰き止める地すべりダムを形成して湛水を生じ、ダムが決壊すれば下流の洪水を起こす。

evidence.quote: Landslides can cause flooding by forming landslide dams that block valleys and stream channels, allowing large amounts of water to back up.

claims.statement: 急で地すべりを起こしやすい地域での地震は地すべりの可能性を大きく高め、1964年のグレートアラスカ地震は広範な地すべりと地盤破壊を起こして地震の金銭的損失の大部分を占めた。

evidence.quote: The occurrence of earthquakes in steep landslide-prone areas greatly increases the likelihood that landslides will occur
The 1964 Great Alaska Earthquake caused widespread landsliding and other ground failure, which caused most of the monetary loss due to the earthquake.

claims.statement: 火山活動による地すべりは最も壊滅的な種類の一つで、溶岩が雪を急速に溶かして生じる岩・土・灰・水の奔流は火山の急斜面で加速し、ラハールと呼ばれる火山性泥流は裾野を離れても遠距離に達する。

evidence.quote: Landslides due to volcanic activity are some of the most devastating types. Volcanic lava may melt snow at a rapid rate, causing a deluge of rock, soil, ash, and water that accelerates rapidly on the steep slopes of volcanoes
These volcanic debris flows (also known as lahars) reach great distances, once they leave the flanks of the volcano

claims.statement: 1980年のワシントンのセント・ヘレンズ山噴火は、火山の北斜面で記録史上最大の地すべりを誘発した。

evidence.quote: The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens, in Washington triggered a massive landslide on the north flank of the volcano, the largest landslide in recorded times.

claims.statement: 人為的原因には斜面やその麓の掘削・載荷・貯水池の水位低下・森林破壊・灌漑・鉱業・人工振動・漏水があり、形態的原因には河川・波・氷河による斜面裾の浸食や火災・干ばつによる植生除去が含まれる。

evidence.quote: a. Excavation of slope or its toe
b. Loading of slope or its crest
d. Deforestation
e. Irrigation
c. Fluvial, wave, or glacial erosion of slope toe or lateral margins
f. Vegetation removal (by fire, drought)

claims.statement: 地すべりは世界中のあらゆる気候・地形条件で発生し、毎年数十億ドルの金銭損失と数千人の死傷をもたらし、長期的な経済混乱・人口移動・自然環境への悪影響を伴うことが多い。

evidence.quote: Landslides occur throughout the world, under all climatic conditions and terrains, cost billions in monetary losses, and are responsible for thousands of deaths and injuries each year. Often, they cause long-term economic disruption, population displacement, and negative effects on the natural environment.

claims.statement: 地すべりは局地的な問題とみなされがちだが、その影響と費用は地方自治体の境界を越えて州や国の問題になりうる。

evidence.quote: Landslides often are characterized as local problems, but their effects and costs frequently cross local jurisdictions and may become State or Provincial or national problems.

claims.statement: 急斜面や既存の地すべり上の建設を避けるか斜面を安定化させることで地すべりの危険は減らせ、滑動体への地下水の上昇を防ぐと安定性が増す。

evidence.quote: The hazard from landslides can be reduced by avoiding construction on steep slopes and existing landslides, or by stabilizing the slopes. Stability increases when ground water is prevented from rising in the landslide mass

claims.statement: 焼け跡の麓や下流は特に急な地形の近くで鉄砲水とデブリフローに弱く、焼けた土は舗装路面のように水をはじくため通常吸収される雨が極めて速く流出する。

evidence.quote: Locations downhill and downstream from burned areas are very susceptible to Flash Flooding and Debris Flows, especially near steep terrain. Rainfall that would normally be absorbed will run off extremely quickly after a wildfire, as burned soil can be as water-repellant as pavement.

claims.statement: デブリフローは乾いた斜面でも激しい雨が数分続けば始まりうる。「激しい」雨とは約1時間に0.5インチの速い降雨で、総雨量より降雨速度が重要である。

evidence.quote: It can start on a dry slope after only a few minutes of intense rain.
"Intense” rain means a burst of rain at a fast rate, about half an inch in an hour. With debris flows, the rainfall rate matters more than total rainfall.

claims.statement: デブリフローは速く予測不能で、人が走るより速く移動でき、開始位置も進路も正確には予測できない。

evidence.quote: Debris flows are fast and unpredictable. They can travel faster than you can run - and they can catch up to your car! Also, no one can say precisely where a debris flow will start or where it will go.

claims.statement: 焼け跡で鉄砲水を生む雨量の目安は1時間未満の0.5インチで、火災の激しさと地形の急さに応じて増減し、焼け跡内の感受性は火災後最初の2年間で最も高い。

evidence.quote: A general rule of thumb is that half an inch of rainfall in less than an hour is sufficient to cause Flash Flooding in a burn area, but this can be more or less depending on the factors above.
The susceptibility to flash flood within the burned area is greatest during the first two years following the fire.

claims.statement: 野火が斜面を焼くと数年間デブリフローの確率が高まり、危険は時間とともにゆっくり低下する。

evidence.quote: When a wildfire burns a slope, it increases the chance of debris flows for several years. The danger does slowly drop over time.

claims.statement: デブリフローを止めたり進路を変えたりすることは誰にもできず、砂袋・暗渠・擁壁は泥と水を誘導できてもデブリフローには通じない。

evidence.quote: No one can stop a debris flow or change its path.
These can help redirect mud and water, but not debris flows.

claims.statement: 他の恒星を回る惑星は「系外惑星」と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: The worlds orbiting other stars are called “exoplanets,” and they come in a wide variety of sizes,

claims.statement: 系外惑星の大きさは、木星より大きいガス巨人から地球や火星ほどの岩石惑星まで幅広い。

evidence.quote: from gas giants larger than Jupiter to small, rocky planets about as big around as Earth or Mars.

claims.statement: 金属を沸騰させるほど高温の系外惑星や、深い凍結状態にあるものがある。

evidence.quote: They can be hot enough to boil metal or locked in deep freeze.

claims.statement: 恒星に極めて近く「1年」が数日しかない系外惑星や、2つの恒星を同時に回るものがある。

evidence.quote: They can orbit their stars so tightly that a “year” lasts only a few days; they can orbit two suns at once.

claims.statement: 恒星を持たず、銀河を永遠の暗闇の中で放浪する系外惑星（ローグ惑星）も存在する。

evidence.quote: Some exoplanets are sunless rogues, wandering through the galaxy in permanent darkness.

claims.statement: 発見された系外惑星の大半は、銀河系の比較的狭い領域に集中している。

evidence.quote: Most of the exoplanets discovered so far are in a relatively small region of our galaxy, the Milky Way.

claims.statement: その「狭い」領域とは太陽系から数千光年以内を指し、1光年は5.88兆マイル（9.46兆キロメートル）に相当する。

evidence.quote: “Small” meaning within thousands of light-years of our solar system; one light-year equals 5.88 trillion miles, or 9.46 trillion kilometers.

claims.statement: 地球に最も近い既知の系外惑星プロキシマ・ケンタウリbは約4光年先にある。

evidence.quote: Even the closest known exoplanet to Earth, Proxima Centauri b, is still about 4 light-years away.

claims.statement: 銀河系には恒星よりも惑星のほうが多いと分かっている。

evidence.quote: We know there are more planets than stars in the galaxy.

claims.statement: 系外惑星の直径と質量の測定から、岩石質からガス質までの組成の幅が見える。

evidence.quote: By measuring exoplanets’ sizes (diameters) and masses (weights), we can see compositions ranging from rocky (like Earth and Venus) to gas-rich (like Jupiter and Saturn).

claims.statement: 水や氷に支配された惑星もあれば、鉄や炭素に支配された惑星もある。

evidence.quote: Some planets may be dominated by water or ice, while others are dominated by iron or carbon.

claims.statement: 溶岩の海に覆われた惑星や、発泡スチロールなみの密度の惑星、母星を回る高密度の核が確認されている。

evidence.quote: We’ve identified lava worlds covered in molten seas, puffy planets the density of Styrofoam and dense cores of planets still orbiting their stars.

claims.statement: 系外惑星はガス巨人、ネプチュニアン、スーパーアース、地球型に分類され、ミニ・ネプチューンなどの下位区分がある。

evidence.quote: So far scientists have categorized exoplanets into the following types: Gas giant, Neptunian, super-Earth, and terrestrial, with subcategories — such as mini-Neptunes — within those groups.

claims.statement: 太陽型恒星を回る最初の系外惑星51ペガシbは1995年10月に特定され、確認済み惑星の数は2025年の節目までに6,000個を超えた。

evidence.quote: The first planet discovered orbiting a Sun-like star, 51 Pegasi b, was identified in October 1995; in the three decades since then, we’ve confirmed 6,000 more, out of billions that we believe exist.

claims.statement: ケプラー宇宙望遠鏡のデータに基づく統計的推定は、銀河系に恒星よりも多くの惑星があることを示した。

evidence.quote: A statistical estimate based on data from NASA’s Kepler Space Telescope revealed that there are more planets than stars in our galaxy.

claims.statement: 銀河系だけで1兆個を超える惑星が存在し、その多くが地球サイズの範囲にあると推定される。

evidence.quote: That means there are more than a trillion planets in our galaxy alone, many of them in Earth’s size range.

claims.statement: 1995年に発見された惑星は、木星の約半分の大きさとみられる高温のガス巨人だった。

evidence.quote: The planet discovered in 1995 was a hot, star-hugging gas giant believed to be about half the size of Jupiter.

claims.statement: その惑星は4日の軌道で母星を力強く引っ張り、星のふらつきが地上の望遠鏡に明白に観測された。

evidence.quote: It tugged so hard on its parent star as it raced around in a four-day orbit that the star’s wobbling was obvious to earthly telescopes — once astronomers knew what to look for.

claims.statement: ふらつき法（視線速度法）は、恒星の「視線速度」の変化を測定する。

evidence.quote: The wobble method measures changes in a star’s “radial velocity.”

claims.statement: 恒星がわずかに近づいたり遠ざかったりするのに伴い、星光の波長は交互に圧縮・伸長される。

evidence.quote: The wavelengths of starlight are alternately squeezed and stretched as a star moves slightly closer, then slightly farther away from us.

claims.statement: その揺れは、公転する惑星からの重力の引きによって生じる。

evidence.quote: Those gyrations are caused by gravitational tugs, this way and that, from orbiting planets.

claims.statement: ケプラー宇宙望遠鏡（2009–2018年）は地球を追う軌道に入り、小さな天域を4年間見続けた。

evidence.quote: The Kepler Space Telescope (2009-2018) ushered in what we could call the “modern” era of planet hunting. Kepler settled into an Earth-trailing orbit, then fixed its gaze on a small patch of sky. It stared at that patch for four years.

claims.statement: その天域には15万個の恒星があり、ケプラーは惑星の通過による微小な減光を待ち受けた。

evidence.quote: Within that small patch were 150,000 stars. Kepler was waiting to catch tiny dips in the amount of light coming from individual stars, caused by planets crossing in front of them.

claims.statement: トランジットで検出されると、惑星の軌道サイズは公転周期と恒星の質量から計算できる。

evidence.quote: Once detected, the planet's orbital size can be calculated from the period (how long it takes the planet to circle once around the star) and the mass of the star.

claims.statement: 2018年に打ち上げられたNASAのトランジット系外惑星探索衛星（TESS）は、同じ手法で全天の広い領域を調査している。

evidence.quote: NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, launched in 2018, employs the same technique (it’s in the name, afterall) to survey whole swaths of our sky.

claims.statement: 分光ではスペクトルの色帯をバーコードのように読み取り、存在する分子を特定できる。

evidence.quote: Scientists can read the color bands of this spectrum like a bar code, revealing which molecules are present.

claims.statement: 重力マイクロレンズは、アインシュタインが最初に記述した効果である、重力が星光を歪め曲げる性質を利用し、手前の恒星が背後の恒星の光を拡大する。

evidence.quote: Another planet-hunting method takes advantage of an effect first described by Einstein: gravity's ability to warp and bend starlight. The gravity of a star in the foreground will magnify the light from a background star that passes just behind it.

claims.statement: NASAの将来のナンシー・グレース・ローマン宇宙望遠鏡は、重力マイクロレンズを用いて系外惑星を発見する計画である。

evidence.quote: NASA’s future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will employ this technique, currently used by ground telescopes, to discover exoplanets.

claims.statement: 直接撮像が捉えるわずかな光は、惑星大気のプロファイルや生命の存在を示唆するガスの証拠を提供し得る。

evidence.quote: But they will provide the next best thing: profiles of exoplanet atmospheres, and perhaps evidence of gases suggesting the presence of life.

claims.statement: ハビタブルゾーンは、惑星が表面に液体の水を持ち得る恒星周りの領域で、「ゴルディロックス・ゾーン」とも呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: The area around a star where its planets could have liquid water on the surface. Also called “Goldilocks zones,” where conditions might be just right — not too hot, not too cold — for life.

claims.statement: 銀河系は重力に束縛された恒星の集まりで、渦を巻きながら宇宙を回転している。

evidence.quote: Our galaxy is a gravitationally bound collection of stars, swirling in a spiral through space.

claims.statement: 観測可能な宇宙には約2兆個の銀河が存在し、銀河系はその一つである。

evidence.quote: Based on the deepest images obtained so far, it’s one of about 2 trillion galaxies in the observable universe.

claims.statement: 銀河系にはおそらく1,000億個から4,000億個の恒星が含まれる。

evidence.quote: Our galaxy probably contains 100 to 400 billion stars, and is about 100,000 light-years across.

claims.statement: 銀河系の直径は約10万光年である。

evidence.quote: Our galaxy probably contains 100 to 400 billion stars, and is about 100,000 light-years across.

claims.statement: 隣の大型銀河アンドロメダは約22万光年の幅を持つ。

evidence.quote: Our neighboring Andromeda galaxy, for example, is some 220,000 light-years wide.

claims.statement: IC 1101と呼ばれる銀河は最大400万光年に達する。

evidence.quote: Another galaxy, IC 1101, spans as much as 4 million light-years.

claims.statement: 光年とは光が1年間に進む距離であり、最もよく使われる天体の物差しの一つである。

evidence.quote: It’s one of the most commonly used celestial yardsticks, the distance light travels in one year.

claims.statement: 光は秒速186,000マイル（30万キロメートル）で進み、1光年は5.8兆マイル（9.5兆キロメートル）に相当する。

evidence.quote: Light zips along through interstellar space at 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second
Multiply that by all the seconds in one year, and you get 5.8 trillion miles (9.5 trillion kilometers).

claims.statement: 地球は太陽から約8光分の距離にある。

evidence.quote: Just for reference, Earth is about eight light minutes from the Sun.

claims.statement: 最も近い隣星プロキシマ・ケンタウリへは、光速でも4.25年かかる。

evidence.quote: Keep going to Proxima Centauri, our nearest neighboring star, and plan on arriving in 4.25 years at light speed.

claims.statement: 銀河系は10万光年を超える恒星の円盤を持つ渦巻銀河である。

evidence.quote: It’s a spiral galaxy with a disk of stars spanning more than 100,000 light-years.

claims.statement: 地球は銀河系の渦巻腕の一つに沿い、中心からほぼ中間に位置する。

evidence.quote: Earth is located along one of the galaxy’s spiral arms, about halfway from the center.

claims.statement: 太陽系は銀河系を1周するのに約2億4,000万年かかる。

evidence.quote: Our solar system takes about 240 million years to orbit the Milky Way just once.

claims.statement: 地球から見ると銀河系は空を横切る淡い乳白色の光の帯に見え、これが名前の由来となった。

evidence.quote: From our perspective on Earth, the Milky Way looks like a faint, milky band of light arcing across the entire sky, which is how it got its name.

claims.statement: その帯は、真横から見た銀河系の中心円盤である。

evidence.quote: This feature marks the central disk of our home galaxy seen edge on.

claims.statement: 銀河系は50以上の銀河からなる局部群（ローカル・グループ）に属している。

evidence.quote: The Milky Way sits in a neighborhood with over 50 other galaxies called the Local Group.

claims.statement: 局部群の構成員は、数十億個までの恒星を持つ矮小銀河から、最も近い大銀河アンドロメダまで幅広い。

evidence.quote: Its members range in size from dwarf galaxies (smaller galaxies with up to a few billion stars) to Andromeda, our nearest large galactic neighbor.

claims.statement: 局部群はおとめ座銀河団の縁のすぐ外側に位置し、ラニアケア超銀河団の一部をなす。

evidence.quote: The Local Group sits just off the edge of the Virgo cluster and is part of the Laniakea supercluster.

claims.statement: スピッツァー宇宙望遠鏡の赤外線画像により、銀河系の渦巻構造は中心の恒星バーの両端から巻き出す2本の腕に支配されていると判明した。

evidence.quote: Using infrared images from NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope, scientists have discovered that the Milky Way's elegant spiral structure is dominated by just two arms wrapping off the ends of a central bar of stars.

claims.statement: それ以前は、銀河系は4本の主腕を持つと考えられていた。

evidence.quote: Previously, our galaxy was thought to possess four major arms.

claims.statement: 2本の主腕はさて座・ケンタウルス腕とペルセウス腕で中心バーの両端に接続し、ノルマ腕といて座腕は主腕の間のあいまいな従腕へ格下げされた。

evidence.quote: The galaxy's two major arms (Scutum-Centaurus and Perseus) can be seen attached to the ends of a thick central bar, while the two now-demoted minor arms (Norma and Sagittarius) are less distinct and located between the major arms.

claims.statement: 主腕には若い星も古い星も最高密度で集まり、従腕は主にガスと散発的な星形成領域で満たされている。

evidence.quote: The major arms consist of the highest densities of both young and old stars; the minor arms are primarily filled with gas and pockets of star-forming activity.

claims.statement: 太陽は、いて座腕とペルセウス腕の間にあるオリオン腕（オリオン・スパー）と呼ばれる小さな部分腕の近くにある。

evidence.quote: Our Sun lies near a small, partial arm called the Orion Arm, or Orion Spur, located between the Sagittarius and Perseus arms.

claims.statement: 銀河系の中心には太陽400万個分の質量を持つブラックホールが鎮座し、大きな銀河の中心には太陽の数十万倍から数十億倍の超大質量ブラックホールがあることが多い。

evidence.quote: Most big galaxies have supermassive black holes at their centers that pack hundreds of thousands to billions of times the Sun’s mass. A black hole weighing 4 million Suns sits in the center of our own galaxy, the Milky Way.

claims.statement: 銀河系と隣の大型銀河アンドロメダは、約45億年後に衝突すると見込まれている。

evidence.quote: Astronomers think the Milky Way and its galactic neighbor Andromeda are set to collide in another 4.5 billion years.

claims.statement: 銀河系は現在も、衛星矮小銀河である大小マゼラン雲から水素の流れを引き寄せていると考えられている。

evidence.quote: Researchers think the Milky Way is currently funneling away a stream of hydrogen from its satellite dwarf galaxies, the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.

claims.statement: 銀河系内のガスの電波調査で「Far-3キロパーセク腕」と呼ばれる新しい腕が見つかっており、2本の主腕より短くバーに沿って位置する。

evidence.quote: The artist's concept also includes a new spiral arm, called the "Far-3 kiloparsec arm," discovered via a radio-telescope survey of gas in the Milky Way. This arm is shorter than the two major arms and lies along the bar of the galaxy.

claims.statement: ケプラー宇宙望遠鏡の観測に基づき、空に見えるすべての恒星がおそらく少なくとも1つの惑星を持つと予測され、数千億の恒星を抱える銀河系の惑星数は数兆個に達し得る。

evidence.quote: we can confidently predict that every star you see in the sky probably hosts at least one planet. Realistically, we’re most likely talking about multi-planet systems rather than just single planets. In our galaxy of hundreds of billions of stars, this pushes the number of planets potentially into the trillions.

claims.statement: 銀河同士が衝突しても恒星同士が激突するとは限らないが、衝突はガス雲を圧縮して新たな星形成を促すことがある。

evidence.quote: Sometimes, galaxies collide. This doesn’t necessarily mean their stars crash – galaxies contain a lot of empty space – but collisions can compress gas clouds, spurring new bouts of star formation.

claims.statement: 互いを通り過ぎるだけの運動量がなければ、衝突した銀河は合体してより大きな1つの銀河を形成する。

evidence.quote: If colliding galaxies don’t have enough momentum to move past each other, they can merge to form a single larger galaxy.

claims.statement: 銀河は、恒星や惑星、ガスと塵の巨大な雲が重力によって束縛された集まりである。

evidence.quote: Galaxies consist of stars, planets, and vast clouds of gas and dust, all bound together by gravity.

claims.statement: 最大の銀河は数兆個の恒星を含み、100万光年を超える広がりを持つ。

evidence.quote: The largest contain trillions of stars and can be more than a million light-years across.

claims.statement: 最小の銀河は数千個の恒星を含み、幅はわずか数百光年である。

evidence.quote: The smallest can contain a few thousand stars and span just a few hundred light-years.

claims.statement: ほとんどの大きな銀河の中心には超大質量ブラックホールがあり、太陽の数十億倍の質量を持つものもある。

evidence.quote: Most large galaxies have supermassive black holes at their centers, some with billions of times the Sun’s mass.

claims.statement: 銀河の形は多様で、多くは渦巻と楕円に分類され、秩序だった姿を持たないものは不規則と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: Galaxies come in a variety of shapes, mostly spirals and ellipticals, as well as those with less orderly appearances, usually dubbed irregular.

claims.statement: ほとんどの銀河の年齢は100億年から136億年の間で、宇宙そのものは約138億年前に形成された。

evidence.quote: Most galaxies are between 10 billion and 13.6 billion years old. Some are almost as old as the universe itself, which formed around 13.8 billion years ago.

claims.statement: 天文学者は、既知で最も若い銀河が約5億年前に形成されたと考えている。

evidence.quote: Astronomers think the youngest known galaxy formed approximately 500 million years ago.

claims.statement: 銀河の分類は形と物理的特徴のほか、超大質量ブラックホールに支えられた中心部の活動性や観測する角度にも基づく。

evidence.quote: Scientists sometimes categorize galaxies based on their shapes and physical features. Other classifications organize galaxies by the activity in their central regions – powered by a supersized black hole – and the angle at which we view them.

claims.statement: 渦巻銀河は渦巻腕で定義される広いクラスで、回転する風車のような平らな恒星の円盤と中心バルジを持つ。

evidence.quote: Our Milky Way is one example of a broad class of galaxies defined by the presence of spiral arms. These galaxies resemble giant rotating pinwheels with a pancake-like disk of stars and a central bulge or tight concentration of stars.

claims.statement: 渦巻銀河は古い恒星・星団・暗黒物質を混ぜたハローに囲まれ、暗黒物質は光を放射も反射もしないが重力を及ぼす。

evidence.quote: Spiral galaxies are surrounded by halos, mixtures of old stars, star clusters, and dark matter – invisible material that does not emit or reflect light but still has a gravitational pull on other matter.

claims.statement: 最も若い星はガスに富む腕で形成され、古い星は円盤やバルジ、ハロー全体に分布する。

evidence.quote: The youngest stars form in gas-rich arms, while older stars can be found throughout the disk and within the bulge and halo.

claims.statement: 銀河系とアンドロメダ銀河は棒渦巻という亜型に属し、棒渦巻は渦巻銀河の3分の2を占める。

evidence.quote: Both the Milky Way and the Andromeda galaxies belong to a subtype known as barred spirals, which make up two-thirds of the group.

claims.statement: 棒は中心を横切る恒星・ガス・塵の帯で、銀河が完全な成熟に達した印と考えられている。

evidence.quote: Barred spirals sport ribbons of stars, gas, and dust that cut across their centers. Scientists think the presence of a bar indicates that a galaxy has reached full maturity.

claims.statement: 楕円銀河は真円から卵形までの形を持ち、渦巻銀河より少ない。

evidence.quote: Elliptical galaxies have shapes that range from completely round to oval. They are less common than spiral galaxies.

claims.statement: 楕円銀河はガスや塵が少なく構造をほとんど持たず、恒星は中心核の周りを不規則な方向に公転し、新しい星を作るガスが乏しいため一般に古い。

evidence.quote: Unlike spirals, elliptical galaxies usually contain little gas and dust and show very little organization or structure. The stars orbit around the core in random directions and are generally older than those in spiral galaxies since little of the gas needed to form new stars remains.

claims.statement: 楕円銀河は渦巻銀河との衝突や合体から生じたと考えられている。

evidence.quote: Scientists think elliptical galaxies originate from collisions and mergers with spirals.

claims.statement: レンズ状銀河は渦巻と楕円の中間で、中心バルジと円盤を持つが腕はなく、古い恒星集団とわずかな星形成しか持たない。

evidence.quote: Lenticular galaxies are a kind of cross between spirals and ellipticals. They have the central bulge and disk common to spiral galaxies but no arms. But like ellipticals, lenticular galaxies have older stellar populations and little ongoing star formation.

claims.statement: 不規則銀河は奇妙な形を持ち、質量は太陽の1億倍の矮小不規則銀河から100億倍の大型まで及ぶ。

evidence.quote: Irregular galaxies have unusual shapes, like toothpicks, rings, or even little groupings of stars. They range from dwarf irregular galaxies with 100 million times the Sun’s mass to large ones weighing 10 billion solar masses.

claims.statement: 不規則銀河の奇妙な形は、他の銀河との相互作用の結果である場合があると考えられている。

evidence.quote: Astronomers think these galaxies’ odd shapes are sometimes the result of interactions with others.

claims.statement: 既知の銀河の約1割は活動銀河で、その中心は全恒星の合計光の100倍以上明るく見える。

evidence.quote: Around 10% of known galaxies are active, which means their centers appear more than 100 times brighter than the combined light of their stars.

claims.statement: 活動銀河の余剰エネルギーは、中心の超大質量ブラックホールの近傍から来ていると考えられている。

evidence.quote: Astronomers think this excess energy comes from areas near the galaxies’ central supermassive black holes, which range from hundreds of thousands to billions of times the mass of our Sun.

claims.statement: ブラックホールの周囲の降着円盤は重力で圧縮・加熱され、赤外線からX線まで複数の波長で輝く。

evidence.quote: Gas and dust collect around the black hole to form an accretion disk. The black hole’s gravity compresses and heats the disk, which causes the material to glow across multiple wavelengths, from infrared to X-rays.

claims.statement: 降着円盤はトーラスと呼ばれる数光年の冷たい塵の環に包まれ、落ち込むガスの一部は光速に近い粒子のジェットとして放出される。

evidence.quote: Infrared observations show that the black hole and its accretion disk are embedded within a clumpy ring of cooler dust, called a torus, that may be a few light-years across. Close to the black hole, a small fraction of the infalling gas can be driven outward, perpendicular to the disk, as jets of particles that move near the speed of light.

claims.statement: 観測された最古の銀河の一部は宇宙が約10億歳の頃に形成され、宇宙の始まりのインフレーションが生んだわずかに密な領域の周りで成長し始めたと考えられている。

evidence.quote: Astronomers know that some of the oldest galaxies observed formed when the universe was only about a billion years old. They think those galaxies started to grow around pockets of space that were slightly denser than their surroundings, an effect created by cosmic inflation when the universe began.

claims.statement: ブラックホールが先か銀河が先かという形成順序は未解決で、ジェイムズ・ウェッブ宇宙望遠鏡の主要な探究目標である。

evidence.quote: It’s possible that the black holes came first, and galaxies grew around them. Or perhaps the galaxies came first, and small black holes within them merged and fed on gas, dust, and stars, eventually becoming the monsters they are today. Exploring this question is a major goal for NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope.

claims.statement: 2004年に公開されたハッブル・ウルトラ・ディープ・フィールドは約1万個の銀河を写し、その一部はビッグバンから8億年以内の130億年前に存在した。

evidence.quote: In 2004, NASA released the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. This image of a small part of the constellation Fornax contains around 10,000 galaxies, some of which existed 13 billion years ago, less than 800 million years after the big bang.

claims.statement: 銀河は約100個以下の群や数千の銀河団にまとまり、超銀河団・ボイド・銀河の壁などが宇宙の物質の網目構造を構成する。

evidence.quote: Galaxies can organize into groups of about 100 or fewer members held together by their mutual gravity. Larger structures, called clusters, may contain thousands of galaxies. Groups and clusters can be arranged in superclusters, which are not gravitationally bound. Superclusters, empty voids, “walls” of galaxies, and other large-scale structures make up the cosmic web of matter in the universe.

claims.statement: 銀河の衝突は恒星の激突を必ずしも意味しないが、ガス雲を圧縮して新たな星形成を促し、銀河系とアンドロメダ銀河は約45億年後に衝突すると見込まれている。

evidence.quote: Sometimes, galaxies collide. This doesn’t necessarily mean their stars crash – galaxies contain a lot of empty space – but collisions can compress gas clouds, spurring new bouts of star formation.
Astronomers think the Milky Way and its galactic neighbor Andromeda are set to collide in another 4.5 billion years.

claims.statement: 互いを通り過ぎる運動量がなければ銀河は合体して1つの大きな銀河になり、渦巻と楕円の合体は不規則銀河を生むこともある。

evidence.quote: If colliding galaxies don’t have enough momentum to move past each other, they can merge to form a single larger galaxy. A merged galaxy can look very different from the two that created it. For example, if a spiral and elliptical merge, the result could be an irregular galaxy.

claims.statement: 大きな銀河は小さな銀河を呑み込んで成長することがあり、銀河系は現在も大小マゼラン雲から水素の流れを引き寄せていると考えられている。

evidence.quote: Larger galaxies can also gobble up smaller ones through proximity and gravitational interactions, pulling material away to fuel their own growth. Researchers think the Milky Way is currently funneling away a stream of hydrogen from its satellite dwarf galaxies, the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.

claims.statement: 超新星は恒星の爆発であり、人類がこれまでに目撃した最大の爆発である。

evidence.quote: A supernova is the biggest explosion that humans have ever seen. Each blast is the extremely bright, super-powerful explosion of a star.

claims.statement: 超新星には、単独の大質量星で起こるものと、連星系で白色矮星への質量移動によって起こるものという2つの異なる型がある。

evidence.quote: there seems to be two distinct types of supernovae -- those which occur for a single massive star and those which occur because of mass transfer onto a white dwarf in a binary system.

claims.statement: 太陽の8倍以上の質量を持つ恒星は、その生涯を超新星として終える。

evidence.quote: Stars which are 8 times or more massive than our Sun end their lives in a most spectacular way; they go supernova.

claims.statement: 恒星は、内側へ押し縮める重力と中心核の核燃焼が生む外向きの圧力という相反する力の均衡によって保たれている。

evidence.quote: A star is in balance between two opposite forces. The star’s gravity tries to squeeze the star into the smallest, tightest ball possible. But the nuclear fuel burning in the star’s core creates strong outward pressure.

claims.statement: 大質量星が燃料を使い果たすと冷却して圧力が下がり、重力が勝って突如崩壊し、巨大な衝撃波が星の外側を爆発させる。

evidence.quote: When a massive star runs out of fuel, it cools off. This causes the pressure to drop. Gravity wins out, and the star suddenly collapses. Imagine something one million times the mass of Earth collapsing in 15 seconds! The collapse happens so quickly that it creates enormous shock waves that cause the outer part of the star to explode!

claims.statement: 崩壊前に星の外側は赤色超巨星へ膨らみ、中心核が鉄だけになると核融合は止まる。鉄を融合しても正味のエネルギーは得られないためである。

evidence.quote: First, the star will swell into a red supergiant...at least on the outside. On the inside, the core yields to gravity and begins shrinking. As it shrinks, it grows hotter and denser.

When the core contains essentially just iron, it has nothing left to fuse. (Because of iron’s nuclear structure, fusing iron does not result in a net yield of energy. Since energy production cannot then be maintained, the star begins to collapse.) Fusion in the core ceases.

claims.statement: 1秒未満で最終的な重力崩壊が始まり、核の温度は1,000億度を超え、核は圧縮後に跳ね返って反動エネルギーが衝撃波を生じさせる。

evidence.quote: In less than a second, the star begins the final phase of gravitational collapse. The core temperature rises to over 100 billion degrees as the iron atoms are crushed together. The repulsive force between the nuclei is overcome by the force of gravity. So the core compresses but then recoils. The energy of the recoil is transferred to the envelope of the star, which then explodes and produces a shock wave.

claims.statement: 衝撃波が外層の物質を加熱して新たな元素や放射性同位体を融合生成し、吹き飛ばされた物質は超新星残骸と呼ばれる。

evidence.quote: As the shock encounters material in the star’s outer layers, the material is heated, fusing to form new elements and radioactive isotopes. The shock then propels that matter out into space. The material that is exploded away from the star is now known as a supernova remnant.

claims.statement: 重力崩壊型ではほぼ中性子だけでできた中性子星が残り、太陽の15倍以上の大質量星ではブラックホールが形成される。

evidence.quote: All that remains of the original star is a small, super-dense core composed almost entirely of neutrons -- a neutron star. Or, if the original star is very massive indeed (say 15 or more times the mass of our Sun), even the neutrons cannot survive the core collapse...and a black hole forms.

claims.statement: 高密度の核とともに、膨張する高温ガスの雲である星雲が残され、太陽の約10倍を超える星の超新星はブラックホールを残すことがある。

evidence.quote: Usually a very dense core is left behind, along with an expanding cloud of hot gas called a nebula. A supernova of a star more than about 10 times the size of our sun may leave behind the densest objects in the universe—black holes.

claims.statement: 白色矮星は太陽の約8倍までの恒星の終点で、質量は太陽の1.4倍未満、大きさは地球ほどである。

evidence.quote: A white dwarf is the endpoint for stars of up to about 8 times that of the Sun. The remaining white dwarf has a mass less than 1.4 times the mass of the Sun, and is about the size of the Earth.

claims.statement: 白色矮星の質量が太陽の1.4倍のチャンドラセカール限界に近づくと、炭素と酸素の核融合が制御不能に始まり星全体の熱核爆発に至る。

evidence.quote: Should the in-falling matter from the companion star cause the white dwarf to approach a mass of 1.4 times that of the Sun (a mass called the Chandrasekhar limit after the scientist who discovered it), the pressure at the center will exceed the threshold for the carbon and oxygen nuclei to start to fuse uncontrollably. This results in a thermonuclear detonation of the entire star.

claims.statement: 熱核爆発後に星は残らず、放射性ニッケルが可視光を含む膨大なエネルギーを放ち、この型の超新星の進展は互いに似通う。

evidence.quote: Nothing is left behind, except whatever elements were left over from the white dwarf or forged in the supernova blast. Among the new elements is radioactive nickel, which liberates huge amounts of energy, including visible light. The evolution of these supernovae tend to all be similar.

claims.statement: 2つ目の型の超新星は、少なくとも1つの地球サイズの白色矮星を含む連星系で、白色矮星同士の衝突や伴星からの過剰な物質の引き込みによって起きる。

evidence.quote: A second type of supernova can happen in systems where two stars orbit one another and at least one of those stars is an Earth-sized white dwarf. A white dwarf is what’s left after a star the size of our sun has run out of fuel. If one white dwarf collides with another or pulls too much matter from its nearby star, the white dwarf can explode.

claims.statement: 超新星は数日から数か月にわたって銀河全体を上回る明るさで輝き、宇宙の彼方からでも観測できる。

evidence.quote: These spectacular events can be so bright that they outshine their entire galaxies for a few days or even months. They can be seen across the universe.

claims.statement: 銀河系のような銀河では1世紀に2〜3個の超新星が起きると考えられ、銀河系外では毎年数百個が観測されるが、宇宙塵が銀河系内の多くの超新星の視界を遮る。

evidence.quote: Astronomers believe that about two or three supernovas occur each century in galaxies like our own Milky Way. Because the universe contains so many galaxies, astronomers observe a few hundred supernovas per year outside our galaxy. Space dust blocks our view of most of the supernovas within the Milky Way.

claims.statement: 科学者は白色矮星を伴う型の超新星を物差しのように用いて宇宙の距離を測る。

evidence.quote: They use the second type of supernova (the kind involving white dwarfs) like a ruler, to measure distances in space.

claims.statement: 金・銀・ウランのような重元素は大質量星だけが作ることができ、爆発的な超新星は蓄積された元素と新たに作られた元素の双方を宇宙へ散布する。

evidence.quote: Only massive stars can make heavy elements like gold, silver, and uranium. When explosive supernovas happen, stars distribute both stored-up and newly-created elements throughout space.

claims.statement: 超新星は星間物質を加熱し、重元素を銀河全体に撒き、宇宙線を加速する。

evidence.quote: They heat up the interstellar medium, distribute heavy elements throughout the Galaxy, and accelerate cosmic rays.

claims.statement: 超新星は星を本質的に破壊する爆発的な噴出であり、新星では噴出が起きても系内の恒星は破壊されない。

evidence.quote: in general, a supernova is an explosive outburst that essentially destroys the star. When a nova occurs, a large outburst takes place, but the stars in the system aren’t destroyed.

claims.statement: 重力崩壊型では大質量星が自ら潰れて衝撃波を生み、Ia型では白色矮星が伴星から得た物質で質量上限を超えて大規模な熱核爆発を起こす。

evidence.quote: In core collapse supernovae, a massive star collapses in on itself and creates a shock wave that produces a bright flash of light. In another class, called Type Ia, a white dwarf gains so much material from a companion that it exceeds the mass limit for white dwarfs, resulting in a massive thermonuclear explosion.

claims.statement: 新星は必ず連星系で起きるが、超新星は連星系でも単独の恒星系でも起きる。

evidence.quote: Novae always take place in binary systems. Supernovae can take place in binary systems or systems with singular stars.

claims.statement: 新星が太陽の数十万倍の明るさなのに対し、超新星は太陽の数十億倍の明るさに達することがある。

evidence.quote: While novae can be hundreds of thousands of times as bright as the Sun, a supernova can be billions of times as bright.

claims.statement: かに星雲は6,500光年先で死んだ大質量星の残骸であり、その超新星は1054年に観測された。

evidence.quote: The Crab Nebula is the leftover, or remnant, of a massive star in our Milky Way that died 6,500 light-years away. Astronomers and careful observers saw the supernova in the year 1054.

claims.statement: NASAのNuSTAR（核分光望遠鏡アレイ）はX線で宇宙を観測し、超新星や若い星雲で爆発前・最中・後の出来事を調べている。

evidence.quote: One example is the NuSTAR (Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array) mission, which uses X-ray vision to investigate the universe. NuSTAR is helping scientists observe supernovas and young nebulas to learn more about what happens leading up to, during, and after these spectacular blasts.

claims.statement: 超新星が放出する高温物質・放射性同位体・中性子星の強磁場中を動く電子はX線とガンマ線を生じ、天体物理学者がこれらの高エネルギー光子を研究に用いる。

evidence.quote: The hot material given off by the supernova, the radioactive isotopes, and the free electrons moving in the strong magnetic field of the neutron star... all of these things produce X-rays and gamma rays. These high-energy photons are used by astrophysicists to study the phenomena of neutron stars and supernovae.
