claims.statement: 星雲は、宇宙空間にある塵とガスの巨大な雲である。

evidence.quote: A nebula is a giant cloud of dust and gas in space.

claims.statement: 一部の星雲は超新星のような死にゆく星の爆発が放出したガスと塵から来ており、他の星雲は新しい星が形成され始めた領域、すなわち「星のゆりかご」である。

evidence.quote: Some nebulae (more than one nebula) come from the gas and dust thrown out by the explosion of a dying star, such as a supernova. Other nebulae are regions where new stars are beginning to form. For this reason, some nebulae are called "star nurseries."

claims.statement: 星雲は主に水素とヘリウムのガスと塵でできている。

evidence.quote: Nebulae are made of dust and gases—mostly hydrogen and helium.

claims.statement: 星雲は星間物質の一部であり、その密度は1立方センチあたり0.1個の原子まで低くなり得る。地球の空気1立方センチには約1,000京個の分子が含まれる。

evidence.quote: These clouds are part of the interstellar medium of extremely low-density gas and dust that exists between stars in the void of space, material so dispersed through the vastness of the cosmos that it can have a density as low as 0.1 atoms per cubic centimeter. In contrast, a cubic centimeter of the air we breathe on Earth would contain about 10 million trillion molecules.

claims.statement: 星雲は、重力がガスと塵を寄せ集めるか、死んだ星が内容物を宇宙へ放出するかして、星間物質が雲を形成するほど密になった場所に生じる。

evidence.quote: Nebulae happen in places where the interstellar medium has become dense enough to form clouds. That could be because gravity has pulled the gas and dust together, or because stars have died and spewed their contents into the cosmos.

claims.statement: 星雲は恒星のライフサイクルの2つの場面、すなわち新しい星の形成と星の死の痕跡に結びついている。

evidence.quote: They’re commonly associated with two parts of the life cycle of stars: First, they can be nurseries forming new baby stars. Second, expanding clouds of gas and dust can mark where stars have died.

claims.statement: 重力は塵とガスの塊をゆっくりと寄せ集め、塊が大きくなるほどその重力は強まる。

evidence.quote: The dust and gases in a nebula are very spread out, but gravity can slowly begin to pull together clumps of dust and gas. As these clumps get bigger and bigger, their gravity gets stronger and stronger.

claims.statement: 塵とガスの塊は自身の重力で崩壊し、中心の物質が加熱され、その高温の核が星の始まりとなる。

evidence.quote: Eventually, the clump of dust and gas gets so big that it collapses from its own gravity. The collapse causes the material at the center of the cloud to heat up-and this hot core is the beginning of a star.

claims.statement: 太陽は45億年以上前に星雲内のガスと塵が重力で集まって誕生し、幼い星の形成には100万年あるいはそれ以上かかることがある。

evidence.quote: Over 4.5 billion years ago, some gas and dust in a nebula clumped together due to gravity, and a baby Sun was born. The process to form a baby star itself can take a million years or more!

claims.statement: 地球に最も近い既知の星雲はヘリックス星雲で、死にゆく星の残骸であり約700光年の距離にある。

evidence.quote: The closest known nebula to Earth is called the Helix Nebula. It is the remnant of a dying star—possibly one like the Sun. It is approximately 700 light-years away from Earth.

claims.statement: 輝線星雲は、恒星の紫外線が水素原子から電子を剥ぎ取る電離を起こし、電子が再結合して低エネルギー状態へ戻るときに光を放つことで輝く。

evidence.quote: This type of nebula forms when the intense radiation of stars within or near the nebula energizes the gas. A star’s ultraviolet radiation floods the gas with so much energy that it strips electrons from the nebula’s hydrogen atoms, a process called ionization. As the energized electrons revert from their higher-energy state to a lower-energy state by recombining with atoms, they emit energy in the form of light, causing the nebula’s gas to glow.

claims.statement: オリオン星雲は、太陽の15〜30倍の質量を持つトラペジウムと呼ばれる4つの大質量星によって照らされている。

evidence.quote: The Orion Nebula is home to a star cluster defined by four massive stars known as the Trapezium. These stars are only a few hundred thousand years old, about 15-30 times the mass of our Sun, and so hot and bright that they’re responsible for illuminating the entire Orion Nebula.

claims.statement: 輝線星雲内の恒星の放射と星風はガスを削り彫刻して洞窟や柱を作り、さらなる星誕生を促す圧力も生む。

evidence.quote: The radiation and solar winds of stars within emission nebulae carve and sculpt the nebula’s gas, creating caverns and pillars but also creating pressures on the gas clouds that can give rise to more starbirth.

claims.statement: 反射星雲は近くの恒星の光を散乱して輝き、照らす星はガスを電離するほど強力ではなく、しばしば青みがかった色に見える。

evidence.quote: Reflection nebulae reflect the light from nearby stars. The stars that illuminate them aren’t powerful enough to ionize the nebula’s gas, as with emission nebulae, but their light scatters through the gas and dust causing it to glow
these reflection nebulae are often bluish in color.

claims.statement: NGC 1999はオリオン星雲の近く約1,500光年の距離にあり、形成直後の恒星V380オリオンisに照らされ、そのガスと塵はその星の形成の残りである。

evidence.quote: A reflection nebula called NGC 1999 lies close to the famous Orion Nebula, about 1,500 light-years from Earth. The nebula is illuminated by a bright, recently formed star called V380 Orionis, and the gas and dust of the nebula is material left over from that star’s formation.

claims.statement: 惑星状星雲は惑星に似て見えたことから名付けられたが惑星とは無関係で、小質量から中質量の星の死の際に外層が放出されて形成され、環・砂時計・長方形など多様な形をなす。その複雑な形の成因はなお研究途上にある。

evidence.quote: Some of the fuzzy objects resembled planets, and these earned the name "planetary nebulae."

Today these nebulae keep the name, but we know they have nothing to do with planets. Planetary nebulae form during the death of low-mass to medium-mass stars. When such stars die, they expel their outer layers into space. These expanding shells of gas form a huge variety of unique shapes – rings, hourglasses, rectangles, and more – that show the complexity of stellar death. Astronomers are still studying how these intricate shapes form at the end of a star’s life.

claims.statement: 惑星状星雲を残した星の中心核は白色矮星となり、太陽ほどの質量を地球サイズで持つブラックホールと中性子星に次ぐ高密度物質で、その紫外線が星雲のガスを電離して輝かせる。

evidence.quote: it leaves behind its core, which becomes a white dwarf star. White dwarf stars are objects with the approximate mass of the Sun but the size of the Earth, making them one of the densest forms of matter in the universe after black holes and neutron stars. The white dwarf star’s ultraviolet radiation ionizes the gas of the planetary nebula and causes it to glow

claims.statement: 太陽はその生涯の終わりに惑星状星雲を形成すると予想されている。

evidence.quote: Our Sun is expected to form a planetary nebula at the end of its life.

claims.statement: 超新星残骸は、星が秒速9,000〜25,000マイルで内容物を放つ超新星爆発で生じ、爆発した星の物質と進路上で巻き込んだ星間物質からなる。

evidence.quote: Some explode in a supernova, flinging their contents into space at anywhere from 9,000 to 25,000 miles (15,000 to 40,000 kilometers) per second.
Supernova remnants consist of material from the exploded star and any interstellar material it sweeps up in its path.

claims.statement: 超新星残骸の輝きはパルサーの星風によって駆動されることがあり、パルサーが放つ電子は磁場と相互作用するシンクロトロン放射によってX線・可視光・電波を生じる。

evidence.quote: Supernova remnants’ glow can also be powered by the stellar wind of a pulsar – a rapidly spinning neutron star created from the core of the exploded star. The pulsar emits electrons that interact with the magnetic field it produces, a process called synchrotron radiation, and emits X-rays, visible light and radio waves.

claims.statement: かに星雲を生んだ1054年の爆発は数週間昼間の空でも見えるほど明るく、星の物質は今も時速約300万マイルで外側へ膨張している。

evidence.quote: The explosion that created it in the year 1054 was so bright that for weeks it could be seen even in the daytime sky, and it was recorded by astronomers across the world. The material from the star is still rushing outward at around 3 million mph (4.8 million kph).

claims.statement: 暗黒星雲（吸収星雲）は光を放射も反射もせず背後の光を遮るガスと塵の雲で、ウィリアム・ハーシェルはこれを「空の穴」と呼んだ。

evidence.quote: Absorption nebulae or dark nebulae are clouds of gas and dust that don’t emit or reflect light, but block light coming from behind them.
Astronomer William Herschel, discussing these seemingly empty spots in the late 1700s, called them “a hole in the sky.”

claims.statement: ボック・グロービュールは小さく冷たいガスと高密度の宇宙塵の雲で、内部で星形成が起きていることを示す温かい核を持つものも見つかっている。

evidence.quote: Included among absorption nebulae are objects like Bok globules, small, cold clouds of gas and dense cosmic dust. Some Bok globules have been found to have warm cores, which would be caused by star formation inside

claims.statement: NASAのスピッツァー宇宙望遠鏡やハッブル宇宙望遠鏡は、多くの遠方の星雲の画像を記録してきた。

evidence.quote: Astronomers use very powerful telescopes to take pictures of faraway nebulae. Space telescopes such as NASA’s Spitzer Space Telescope and Hubble Space Telescope have captured many images of faraway nebulae.

claims.statement: ジェイムズ・ウェッブ宇宙望遠鏡は主に赤外線で観測し、塵とガスの雲の深部を見通して星と惑星系の形成を研究している。

evidence.quote: The James Webb Space Telescope primarily observes the infrared universe. With Webb, scientists are peering deep into clouds of dust and gas to study how stars and planetary systems form.

claims.statement: チャンドラX線天文台は、かに星雲で超新星として爆発した星のつぶれた都市サイズの核であるパルサーからの高エネルギーX線を捉えている。

evidence.quote: In the Crab Nebula, Chandra sees high-energy X-rays from a pulsar (a type of rapidly spinning neutron star, which is the crushed, city-sized core of a star that exploded as a supernova).

claims.statement: 太陽の生涯全体は直接観測できないため、科学者は異なる段階にある膨大な数の恒星や星雲を調べて太陽の来歴と行方を推論している。

evidence.quote: Since the Sun will live so much longer than us, scientists can’t observe its whole life cycle directly … but they can study tons of other stars and nebulae at different phases of their lives and draw conclusions about where our Sun came from and where it’s headed.
